sentences.text: Manual resolution begins when an image or identity exception prevents automatic processing from establishing a reliable disposition.
Image Resolution Desk presents the available bag image and exception details to the operator for review.
The operator compares visible bag features with the recorded tag number and the handling data associated with the bag.
The operator confirms that the image is legible enough to support a decision and does not rely on an uncertain visual match.
Image Resolution Desk uses the rescan receipt to confirm that a second image was captured under the approved procedure.
When the image remains inconclusive, the operator requests a physical inspection through the established inspection process.
The identity check verifies that the physical tag is attached to the inspected bag and that its number agrees with the recorded bag identity.
Baggage Control System checks the recorded bag identity against the current routing data before any disposition is committed.
Flight Data Gateway provides the flight data used to validate the bag's assigned destination and service date.
Bag Reconciliation Station records whether the inspected bag matches the expected flight assignment.
A mismatch places the bag on hold until an authorized operator resolves the discrepancy or escalates it.
Juniper holds the affected bag from automatic sorting while the manual disposition remains unresolved.
Kestrel captures a readable tag image when the bag is presented for a permitted scan.
North Gate Scanner records the tag read and image data needed to support an operator's identity check.
Secondary Inspection Chute provides a controlled location for bags requiring physical examination.
Explosives Response Team conducts any security examination assigned under applicable procedures.
Baggage Operations Supervisor approves the operational disposition when the case exceeds the operator's authority.
After the identity and flight checks pass, Baggage Control System authorizes the bag to rejoin its previously assigned screening and sort path.
Outbound Load Control Desk confirms that the bag remains eligible for inclusion in the planned flight load.
Airline Ramp Coordinator confirms any flight-side constraint that could prevent the reconciled bag from being accepted.
Concourse Zone Controller applies the authorized routing state without bypassing required screening controls.
Maintenance Technician uses the witness tag to verify that the applicable calibration status was witnessed before equipment returns to service.
If a route or flight assignment has changed, the operator obtains approval before the bag is released into the revised process.
The final disposition and supporting checks are recorded so that later review can trace why the bag returned to the planned process.
